sections.heading: 1. How to choose
lines: ① Fresh sprain or knock: ice, first 1–2 days.
② Stiff, achy or tight muscles: heat.
③ Wrap it in a cloth, 10–15 min at a time.
④ Then gentle movement does the real work.

sections.heading: 2. Skip it and get checked if…
lines: Skin is numb — no heat or ice there,
and you can't take weight on the leg.

slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Toto rolled an ankle and is stuck between ice pack and heat pack. Hybi's honest answer: it matters less than you think.

As a rough guide, ice suits fresh sprains and knocks in the first couple of days, wrapped in a cloth for 10–15 minutes. Heat tends to suit stiffness and tight muscles, especially before you get moving.

Current guidelines suggest neither one speeds healing much on its own. They're comfort tools, so pick whichever helps you move more easily, and pair it with gentle movement.

Get checked if you can't take weight on the leg, there's big swelling or an odd shape, or numbness or colour change. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio 🐰
